# fit-push module manuals

User manuals of all installed modules, collected from `modules/<id>/MANUAL.md`.

## All activities map

*Module `activity_map` v1.0.0 · owner @m-luk*


### What it does

Shows the routes of all your activities with GPS on one large map. You can narrow
it down by sport, by tag and by date, and colour the routes either by sport (to see
where you ride versus run) or by date (to see where you trained recently versus
long ago). Clicking a route opens that activity.

### How to use

1. Click **🗺️ Map** in the navigation bar at the top (next to Activities and Segments).
2. All routes appear, zoomed to fit. Hover a route to see its name, date and
   distance; it is highlighted. Click it to open the activity.
3. **Sports**: click one or more sport chips to show only those sports. Click a
   chip again to remove it; with no chip pressed, all sports are shown. Each chip's
   colour square is the colour of that sport's routes.
4. **Tags**: works the same way with your activity tags (add tags on an activity
   page under its title). Only shown when you have tags.
5. **Dates**: pick a preset (*Last 30 days*, *This year*, …) or set **from** /
   **to** dates for a custom range.
6. **Colour by**: *Sport* uses one colour per sport (legend bottom-left);
   *Date* goes from light blue (oldest shown) to dark blue (newest), with the date
   span in the legend.
7. The filters are part of the page address, so you can bookmark a view (for
   example "gravel rides this year").

### Limitations

- Only activities with GPS are shown (indoor and pool sessions are skipped).
- Routes are simplified to about one point every 25 m for speed; open the activity
  for the full-resolution track.
- Up to 8 sports get their own colour; any further sports share a gray "Other".
- At most 2000 routes are drawn at once; narrow the filters if you have more.
- The map tiles come from OpenStreetMap, so viewing the map shares the map area
  with their tile servers, as on any activity page.

## Adventures

*Module `adventures` v0.1.0 · owner @m-luk*


### What it does

Groups several activities into one **adventure** and shows them together: one map,
totals for the whole trip, a row per day, the fastest and slowest day (by average
speed), the longest and shortest day, the highest point, the day with the biggest climb,
and averages per day and per activity.

There are two types:

- **Traverse**: one continuous line that goes somewhere (a bikepacking trip, a
  long-distance hike): every activity starts where the previous one ended (within 1 km by
  default), and at least half of them end away from where they started. A loop from the
  camp in between is fine; a gap such as a bus ride makes it multi-day.
- **Multi-day**: every other trip: outings from one base on consecutive days (a ski week,
  a climbing trip from a hut), or moving between places with gaps.

The module also looks through your activities and **proposes** adventures it finds.
Activities of different sports can be mixed, and activities tagged `#commute` are
left out unless you change that.

### How to use

1. Open **Adventures** in the navigation bar. Your saved adventures show at once; below
   them, **Proposed adventures** appear when detection finishes ("Looking for adventures
   in your activities…" until then). Each row shows the type, the dates, the place (📍,
   filled in as it is found), the number of days and activities and the distance.
   Click **▸** at the start of a row to unfold it: you see its activities (each links to
   the activity) and a small map; **Find place again** repeats the place lookup.
2. Click **Create** on a proposal. The name is proposed from the place found on
   OpenStreetMap as
   `YYYY-MM Park, City` (for example `2026-07 Tatra National Park, Zakopane`); without a
   national park the mountain range takes its place (`2026-08 Julian Alps, Bovec`). When
   nothing is found, the name comes from the type and dates. Keep or change it and click **Create** again.
   Click **Dismiss** to hide a proposal for good (**Show dismissed proposals again**
   brings dismissed ones back).
3. To build one by hand, click **New adventure**, enter a name, then tick the activities
   in the list that opens. Change **from** / **to** to see other dates, and click
   **Save**.
4. In an adventure, the tiles show the totals, the **Highest point**, the **Longest day**
   and the **Biggest climb** (most elevation gain in one day). **Colour by** switches the
   map between **Activity** (each activity its own colour, in day order), **Day** (one
   colour per day) and **Total** (the whole route in one colour), or, like the activity
   map, colours the route by **Elevation**, **Speed** (**Pace** for running and walking) or
   **Heart rate**, light to dark from low to high (the legend shows the range). A measure
   with no data is greyed out. Click **Day 1**, **Day 2**, … or
   a row of the **Per day** table to focus the map on one day; **All days** shows
   everything again. Click a route to open the activity.
5. Use the **Traverse** / **Multi-day** buttons to change the type, **Rename** to change
   the name, **Find place** to look up the park, mountain range and city (and rename the adventure to
   them if you like), **Edit activities** to add or remove activities, and **Delete** (click
   twice) to remove the adventure. Deleting an adventure keeps its activities.
6. Click **Detection settings** on the Adventures page to change what is proposed:
   - **Max days without activity between days** (default 1): how many empty days may
     lie between two days of one adventure.
   - **Traverse: each start within … of the previous end** (default 1 km): how close an
     activity must start to where the previous one ended for the trip to count as one
     continuous line.
   - **Same place: a start within … of an earlier start or end** (default 2 km): how near
     an activity must start to the trip so far to belong to it.
   - **Minimum days** (default 2).
   - **Ignore home** (default 8 weeks): a place where you start activities in this many
     different weeks counts as home and does not link activities, so your everyday
     training is not proposed. 0 turns it off.
   - **Excluded tags** (default `commute`) and **Sports that count** (none ticked = any
     sport).
   - **Use OpenStreetMap for place names** (on by default): see Limitations.

   Click **Save and detect** to apply (the settings close), or **Restore defaults**.
7. On an activity page, the **Adventure** line under the title links to the adventures
   the activity belongs to, with its day number.

### Limitations

- Place names come from OpenStreetMap. To find them, one point in the middle of the
  route (rounded to about 100 m) is sent to the OpenStreetMap Overpass API for each
  proposal shown on the Adventures page (each place is looked up once and remembered),
  and when you click **Find place**. If you click **Create** before the place is found,
  the name comes from the type and dates. Turn off **Use OpenStreetMap for place
  names** in the detection settings to never send anything. Place names need the
  **OpenStreetMap places** module (loaded by default); without it the option is greyed out. The lookup needs an internet
  connection and can take a few seconds; national parks are found when the route's
  middle is inside one or within 25 km of its centre, mountain ranges when it is inside
  one or within 60 km of where OpenStreetMap places the range (often a label point or a
  ridge line, so a large range may be missed or a neighbouring one chosen).
- Detection needs GPS and a start time; activities without GPS can still be added by
  hand (they count in the totals but have no line on the map).
- Days are calendar days of the recorded start time (UTC), so a late-evening activity
  in a far time zone may fall on the next day.
- Activities already in an adventure are not proposed again.
- A trip to a place you visit very often (more weeks than **Ignore home**) is treated as
  home and not proposed; lower the setting or create the adventure by hand.
- Fastest and slowest day compare average speeds, even when the days have different
  sports.

## Gear

*Module `gear` v0.4.1 · owner @m-luk*


### What it does

Keeps track of your equipment (shoes, bikes, skis, boats and anything else) and how
much you have used it: total distance, moving time, number of activities and the last
time you used it. Give an item a distance limit and a bar shows when it is due for
replacement. Pick a default gear for a sport (e.g. Running) or for a whole group of
sports (e.g. All cycling), and every new activity of that sport gets it automatically.

### How to use

1. Open **Gear** in the navigation bar at the top and click **Add gear**.
2. Enter a **Name**, choose the **Kind**, and optionally a **Starting distance** (what
   the item had before you started tracking it) and **Replace after** (the distance
   limit). Add **Notes** if you like.
3. Under **Default for**, tick the sports or sport groups (**All cycling**, **All
   running**, …) that should use this item, then click **Save**. Each sport or group has
   one default per kind: ticking one that another item of the same kind holds (shown as
   "now …") moves it to this item. A sport's own default beats its group's, so you can
   set a road bike for **All cycling** and an MTB for **Mountain biking**.
4. Activities you imported before setting defaults have no gear: click **Apply
   defaults** in the notice at the top of the **Gear** page.
5. To give gear to many activities at once, click **No gear (N)** at the top of the
   **Gear** page. It lists every activity without gear; narrow it with the sport
   filter, tick activities (click a row, **Shift**+click for a range, or the box in the
   header for all shown), pick an item and click **Add to selected**. Click **Gear** to
   go back to your items.
6. On an activity page, the **Gear** line under the title shows its gear. Click
   **Change** (or **Add**), tick the items you used and click **Save**. **Reset** undoes
   a manual choice; click an item to open the **Gear** page.
7. When an item is worn out, click **Retire**: it keeps its history but is no longer
   assigned automatically. **Unretire** brings it back; **Delete** (click twice) removes
   it and its history.

### Limitations

- Defaults apply to new imports and to sport changes; changing a default never rewrites
  activities that already have gear. A gear choice made by hand is kept when you change
  the activity's sport.
- Distance and time come from the activity summary, so indoor activities without
  distance add only time.
- Trimmed copies (clips) get the default gear of their sport, not the gear of the
  original activity.

## OpenStreetMap places

*Module `osm_places` v0.1.0 · owner @m-luk*


### What it does

Finds the national park, the mountain range and the nearest city or town around a place
on your activities, using OpenStreetMap. It has no page of its own: other modules use it,
for example **Adventures** to name a trip "2026-07 Tatra National Park, Zakopane".

### How to use

1. Nothing to set up. Keep this module enabled (it is by default) for the modules that
   use it to show place names; the **Modules** page lists it as loaded.
2. Turn lookups on or off in the module that uses them (for Adventures:
   **Detection settings** → **Use OpenStreetMap for place names**).
3. To stop all lookups at once, start fit-push without this module, for example
   `python scripts/run.py --modules adventures,gear` (every module except this one).

### Limitations

- Needs an internet connection; a lookup takes a few seconds and runs at most once per
  second.
- Each lookup sends one point, rounded to about 100 m, to the OpenStreetMap Overpass API.
  Answers are remembered per point, so the same place is not asked again.
- OpenStreetMap often maps a mountain range as a label point or a ridge line, so a large
  range may be missed or a neighbouring one chosen; parks are found when the point is
  inside one or within 25 km of its centre.

## Strava import

*Module `strava_import` v0.1.1 · owner @m-luk*


### What it does

Reads the zip you download from Strava ("Download your data") and brings it into
fit-push: activities you don't have yet are imported, and the ones you already have
(uploaded earlier from your watch or bike computer) are recognised and updated with what
you set on Strava: the title, the sport type, the bike or shoes, the commute flag, the
description and your private note.

### How to use

1. On strava.com open **Settings → My Account → Download or Delete Your Account →
   Request your archive**, and download the zip from the e-mail Strava sends.
2. Open the **Strava import** page and choose the zip in **Export zip**.
3. Under **Bring over**, untick what you don't want (for example **Titles** if you
   prefer your own names).
4. Click **Preview**. Nothing changes yet: the report shows how many activities are
   already here, how many would be imported, and every change per activity.
5. Click **Import** to apply. Large exports take a few minutes. Reload the page
   afterwards so the activity list shows the new activities and titles.
6. Open an activity: the **Strava** card shows its description, private note and an
   **Open on Strava** link. Bikes and shoes appear on the **Gear** page (with the
   **Gear** module) with the default sports you chose on Strava.

Running the import again with a newer export is safe: activities are never imported
twice and only real changes are applied.

### Limitations

- An activity is recognised when the file is identical or starts within 60 seconds of
  one you have; activities without a file on Strava (entered by hand) are skipped.
- A plain Strava "Ride" never replaces a more specific sport you already have (road,
  gravel or mountain biking).
- Activity types are understood in English and Polish exports; other types are listed
  in the report and the sport is left as it is.
- Photos, comments, kudos, segments, routes and clubs are not imported.
- Gear needs the **Gear** module; imported gear assignments count as a manual choice.
